question.text:
Consider the following C code segment:
 

#include <unistd.h>
#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
    int i;
    for (i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        pid_t pid = fork();
        
        if (pid == 0) {
            // Child branch
            printf("Child %d created in iteration %d\n", getpid(), i);
            break; // Exit the loop only for the child process
        } else {
            // Parent branch
            printf("Parent %d created child %d in iteration %d\n", getpid(), pid, i);
        }
    }
    
    sleep(1);
    return 0;
}


Assuming all $\verb|fork()|$ calls succeed, what is the total number of processes (including the original parent) that will be running immediately before the program terminates?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a file system utilizing a FAT (File Allocation Table) where the overhead associated with each entry in the FAT is $\mathbf{4}$ bytes. If the file system is deployed on a massive $2 \times 10^{12}$ bytes disk and the data block size is set to $8 \times 10^3$ bytes, determine the maximum possible file size that can be stored on this disk in units of TB (Terabytes). (Note: $1 \mathrm{~TB}=10^{12}$ bytes).

  1. $1.999$
     
  2. $1999$
     
  3. $2.3$
     
  4. $1.898$

question.text:
A FAT (File Allocation Table) based file system is being used. The total overhead of each entry in the FAT is $\mathbf{8 ~bytes}$ in size. Given a $50 \times 10^9 ~\textbf{bytes}$ disk on which the file system is stored and a data block size of $4 \times 10^3~\textbf{byte}$, the maximum size of a file that can be stored on this disk in units of MB (Megabytes) is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Note: $1 ~\mathrm{MB}=10^6~\text{bytes}$).
